section_summary: This section assembles U.S. and Allied intelligence on Japan’s wartime access to petroleum, metals, machinery, foodstuffs, shipping, and industrial capacity. It includes detailed inventories of Japanese military-industrial facilities, a British assessment of resources obtainable from Indochina and Thailand, and inquiries into European machine-tool suppliers. The later documents investigate suspected Chilean and Mexican schemes to supply Japan with copper, scrap metal, molybdenum, mercury, petroleum, and other strategic materials through diplomatic or commercial intermediaries.

subfiles.title: The Export of Petroleum Products to Japan
subfiles.from: Charles W. Yost, Department of State
subfiles.to: Internal distribution: EA, FE, TA, and PA/H
subfiles.about: Assesses petroleum exports to Japan and recommends broader export licensing and tighter quantitative restrictions.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum argues that existing and pending licenses would give Japan gasoline supplies far above normal prewar imports, including fuel suitable for aviation after minimal processing. It also warns that aviation lubricants may be crossing Siberia to Germany and discusses risks involving diesel oil and crude oil. Yost recommends redefining aviation gasoline and lubricants, licensing all petroleum products, limiting several categories to prewar quantities, and consulting the British.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on aviation-gasoline definitions
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Controls (Yost)
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum enclosing technical definitions of aviation gasoline by Edgar and Wilson.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: memorandum 800.6363/654 with two proposed aviation-gasoline definitions by Mr. Edgar and Dr. Wilson.

subfiles.title: Information Affecting Japan’s War Strength as of the Beginning of 1940
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.to: Adolf A. Berle, Jr., Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Transmits statistics copied from a Japanese yearbook belonging to detained Domei representative Masuo Kato.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure inventories Japanese shipping, airfields, naval bases, aircraft and arms plants, radio stations, divisional headquarters, warships, fortified zones, and major defense industries. It also supplies company capitalization and defense-expenditure figures. The information was shared with the Coordinator of Information, Naval Intelligence, and Military Intelligence.

subfiles.title: Exports of Tin-Plate Scrap to Japan, 1933–1941
subfiles.about: Provides annual quantity and value data for U.S. tin-plate-scrap exports to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The letter explains that national-defense policy required retaining all domestic and imported tin-plate scrap for U.S. industry. Export licenses were therefore withheld for 1941, and exports had been prohibited since December 31, 1940. The attached table records declining Japanese purchases from 1933 through 1940 and none for 1941.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese payment for oil shipments
subfiles.about: Points to a Treasury memorandum on a proposed Japanese method for paying for oil shipments.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference: memorandum requesting State's views on Japanese oil-payment arrangements, filed in Frozen Credits.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on Japanese payment for oil shipments
subfiles.about: Points to a Treasury letter concerning a proposed Japanese method of paying for oil shipments.
subfiles.summary: Second cross-reference on the Japanese oil-payment arrangement letter in the Frozen Credits file.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs summary of an article on Japan’s war economy
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Basel newspaper’s account of Axis-country views concerning Japan’s war economy.
subfiles.summary: Far Eastern Affairs summary: the article minimizes Japanese gains in China but notes better results in Manchuria and Southeast Asia, shipping and steel shortages, and a Singapore shipbuilding plan; judged superficial but useful.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 113: “Slightest Discontinuance in Japanese Armament Production Should Ruin that Country”
subfiles.from: Walter H. Sholes, American Consul General, Basel
subfiles.about: Forwards an English translation of an article on the Japanese war effort.
subfiles.summary: Despatch 113: Sholes encloses a translation from Basel's Arbeiter Zeitung, from Pester Lloyd, 'Slightest Discontinuance in Japanese Armament Production Should Ruin that Country'; copies to Bern and Zürich.

subfiles.title: “Exploitation of China” and Japan’s wartime economic position
subfiles.about: Analyzes Japan’s ability to exploit conquered territories and sustain war production.
subfiles.summary: Translated article doubts Japan's lasting gains from occupied China but sees Manchukuo as cooperative and gains in Indochina, Thailand and Burma, doubting Singapore shipbuilding; steel shortages could imperil Japan.

subfiles.title: Military attaché forwarding report on Japanese economic gains in Indochina and Thailand
subfiles.about: Forwards a British economic-warfare study of resources available to Japan in Indochina and Thailand.
subfiles.summary: Military attaché forwards a British study of Japan's raw material and food gains in Indochina and Thailand, noting rice, rubber, tin, tungsten and others and transport constraints.

subfiles.title: Indo-China and Thailand
subfiles.doc_type: British economic intelligence report with map
subfiles.to: British and American intelligence and economic agencies
subfiles.about: Estimates the quantities and strategic significance of materials Japan could obtain from Indochina and Thailand.
subfiles.summary: The report concludes that Japan had secured its current rice, rubber, and tin needs and most of its tungsten requirements from the two territories. It describes further potential in zinc, chrome, manganese, phosphates, antimony, bauxite, iron, hides, and teak, but stresses difficult transportation and development. It finds that the territories cannot remedy Japan’s shortages of oil, nickel, copper, and lead, and includes a map of principal agricultural and mineral zones.

subfiles.title: Chilean activities concerning scrap metal
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Reports an alleged Chilean plan to collect scrap metal in the Americas for clandestine delivery to Japan.
subfiles.summary: FBI source alleges Chilean chargés arranged scrap purchases through Chilean firms, to travel on Chilean ships and transfer to Japanese vessels, with pouches used to evade censorship.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference on the Kawanishi aircraft works
subfiles.about: Points to Economic Warfare Intelligence report No. 26 on the Kawanishi aircraft works.
subfiles.summary: The sheet links the equipment-and-supplies file to despatch No. 4611. The referenced report concerns Japan’s Kawanishi aircraft works.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 3791 requesting information on European machinery and automotive exports to Japan
subfiles.from: Department of State for the Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Requests detailed intelligence on European machine tools and automotive components formerly supplied to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 3791 seeks manufacturer names, shipment dates, capacities and Japanese recipients of European machine tools and automotive parts, especially after 1935; lists known suppliers; parallel inquiries to Bern and Stockholm.

subfiles.title: Board of Economic Warfare draft cable to London
subfiles.from: William T. Stone, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Requests transmission to James Somerville of the machinery-and-automotive-parts inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Board of Economic Warfare draft cable to London holds the full instructions later sent as telegram 3791.

subfiles.title: Telegram to Bern requesting machinery and automotive-parts intelligence
subfiles.from: Department of State for the Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Requests information on European machinery and components supplied to Japanese vehicle manufacturers.
subfiles.summary: Telegram to Bern asks for data on specialized machine tools and automotive parts formerly exported to Japan; surviving copy ends mid-request.

subfiles.title: Damaged Board of Economic Warfare draft cable to Bern
subfiles.about: Drafts a request for Swiss-source information on machinery and automotive parts supplied to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Damaged Board of Economic Warfare draft cable to Bern repeating the inquiry into European suppliers and Japanese recipients; parts illegible.

subfiles.title: Board of Economic Warfare cable request to Bern
subfiles.from: William T. Stone, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Requests dispatch of the machinery-and-automotive-parts inquiry to the American Legation in Bern.
subfiles.summary: BEW cable request to Bern stressing engine bearings, axles, gears, spark plugs, brakes and specialized machinery; names European suppliers.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 59 requesting Bern’s reply
subfiles.from: Department of State for the Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Asks when a reply may be expected to the August machinery inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 59 follows up Department telegram 1943 of August 11 and asks when Bern's information will arrive.

subfiles.title: Draft follow-up telegram to Bern
subfiles.from: Board of Economic Warfare, Document Security Section
subfiles.about: Requests dispatch of a reminder to the American Legation in Bern.
subfiles.summary: Draft follow-up to Bern asking an answer to the August 11 telegram; William Stone approved it, sent November 19.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 668 requesting machinery and automotive-parts intelligence from Stockholm
subfiles.from: Department of State for the Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Requests Swedish and European information about specialized machinery and automotive parts supplied to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The telegram asks for manufacturers, shipment dates and quantities, machine capacities, end uses, and Japanese customers, concentrating on the period after 1935. It identifies several German, Austrian, Swedish, and Swiss suppliers and notes similar inquiries to Bern and London.

subfiles.title: Board of Economic Warfare draft cable to Stockholm
subfiles.from: William T. Stone, Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of the industrial-supply inquiry to the American Legation in Stockholm.
subfiles.summary: Board of Economic Warfare draft cable to Stockholm requesting data on machinery and automotive components sent to Japan, listing known continental suppliers.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 1014 requesting Stockholm’s reply
subfiles.from: Department of State for the Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Asks when Stockholm will answer the Department’s August industrial-information request.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 1014 asks Stockholm when it may expect the reply to Department telegram 668 of August 11.

subfiles.title: Draft follow-up request to James Somerville
subfiles.from: Board of Economic Warfare, Document Security Section
subfiles.about: Requests a reminder to James Somerville in London concerning the August machinery inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Draft follow-up asking the State Department to request a reply to telegram 3791 of August 11, from Economic Warfare Analysis.

subfiles.title: Telegram No. 5801 requesting London’s reply
subfiles.from: Department of State for the Board of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Asks when information requested in the August machinery telegram may be expected.
subfiles.summary: The telegram refers to Department telegram No. 3791 of August 11 and requests a status report. Page 211 is a nearly blank or badly reproduced Board of Economic Warfare routing copy associated with the message.

subfiles.title: Chilean activities concerning scrap metal
subfiles.from: J. Edgar Hoover, Federal Bureau of Investigation
subfiles.about: Provides another filed copy of the report alleging a Chilean scrap-metal collection scheme for Japan.
subfiles.summary: FBI memorandum alleging Chilean diplomats sought scrap across Latin America through intermediaries, to pass from Chilean ships to Japanese vessels, using diplomatic pouch.

subfiles.title: Instruction quoting the FBI report on Chilean scrap metal
subfiles.about: Sends the alleged Chilean-Japanese scrap scheme to the embassy for comment.
subfiles.summary: Instruction quoting the FBI report on Chilean scrap purchases through third parties, Pacific transshipment and use of the diplomatic pouch to evade Canal Zone censorship.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on a possible Japanese ship for Chilean copper
subfiles.about: Calls for investigation and an instruction to Santiago concerning a possible secret Japanese copper shipment.
subfiles.summary: Berle reports Japan may send a vessel to a Chilean port under safe conduct to load copper; asks that the FBI be consulted and Santiago watch for direct or island transshipment.

subfiles.title: Confidential instruction No. 1994 to Santiago
subfiles.about: Requests embassy comment on suspected secret Chilean metal shipments to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Instruction 1994 to Santiago on a possible Japanese-Chilean copper or scrap-iron deal, perhaps via a third country or island, and safe-conduct talks for a Japanese vessel.

subfiles.title: Despatch transmitting conversations on Japanese interest in Chilean copper
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, aboard M/S Gripsholm
subfiles.about: Transmits two staff memoranda based on conversations with former Chilean diplomats in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Grew forwards reports by Carl H. Boehringer and Donald W. Lamm about Japanese efforts to obtain Chilean copper and arrange wartime trade. He notes that a summary had already been telegraphed through the embassy at Rio de Janeiro along with information about a possible Japanese threat to South America.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Japanese interest in Chilean copper
subfiles.about: Records Guillermo de la Jara’s warnings about Japan’s need for Chilean copper and possible aggressive measures to obtain it.
subfiles.summary: De la Jara says Chilean ore refines Japan's low-grade copper and Japanese stocks last six months; Japanese discussed attacking the Panama Canal or Chilean copper centers; a Foreign Ministry official asked about Easter Island water.

subfiles.title: Conversations between the Chilean commercial counselor and the Japanese Foreign Office
subfiles.about: Records Japanese-Chilean proposals for exchanging copper or nitrate for Japanese cement or rubber.
subfiles.summary: Cuadros says Takata and Kawasaki proposed Valparaíso as an exchange point for cement against copper, which he refused as strategic; a nitrate-for-rubber plan failed over Army objection to resale to the US.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Grew despatch on strategic materials from Mexico
subfiles.to: Military Intelligence Division and Office of Naval Intelligence
subfiles.about: Forwards a photostatic copy of Grew’s despatch on strategic-material shipments from Mexico to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Department sends military and naval intelligence Grew's August 20 despatch on Mexico and enclosures, hoping they prove useful.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on Grew’s Mexico despatch
subfiles.about: Explains the delayed handling and significance of Grew’s report on strategic materials sent from Mexico to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum recounts how Zavala obtained letters implicating former Salvadoran consul general Sigüenza in purchases of molybdenum, mercury, and other materials for Japanese interests. Delivery of the despatch was delayed until Zavala could report through the Nicaraguan government. Copies were supplied to relevant State Department divisions for field action.

subfiles.title: Direct transmittal of Grew’s Mexico despatch to FC
subfiles.about: Sends a carbon copy of Grew’s strategic-materials despatch directly to avoid routing delay.
subfiles.summary: Note: Grew's Mexico strategic-materials despatch is sent directly to avoid the usual delay.

subfiles.title: Shipment from Mexico to Japan of Strategic Materials
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, aboard M/S Gripsholm
subfiles.about: Forwards evidence concerning Mexican shipments of mercury, molybdenum, and other strategic materials to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Grew: Zavala, after taking over the Salvadoran consulate in Tokyo, received mail for Petróleos Leon's Abraham Phillips showing Japanese Army and Navy purchases via Mitsubishi Shoji and Showa Tsusho; recommends investigation.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation with Consul General Zavala
subfiles.about: Describes how Zavala acquired letters exposing a covert Mexican supply network for Japan.
subfiles.summary: Zavala says Petróleos Leon was a cover for shipping molybdenum, copper, mercury and other metals to Japan, including a Manzanillo-Shanghai plan and an alleged mercury shipment by submarine.

subfiles.title: Summary of Petróleos “Leon” correspondence
subfiles.about: Summarizes correspondence documenting Petróleos “Leon” transactions with Japanese military purchasers.
subfiles.summary: Summary of Petróleos Leon papers: staff, ships and intermediaries for the Japanese Army and Navy; prepaid order for 100 tons of molybdenum; demand for metals and oil; censorship evasion through captains and diplomatic mail.

subfiles.title: Letter from the Tokyo office of Petróleos “Leon” to Abraham Z. Phillips
subfiles.about: Acknowledges delayed correspondence and begins discussing shipments, communications, and Army payment for molybdenum.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo office of Petróleos Leon tells Phillips documents arrived on the Heiyo Maru, asks that papers go via ship captains, and begins explaining the $134,300 Army advance for molybdenum; continues.
